event_overview.title: About US Midterm Elections
event_overview.subject: US Midterm Elections
event_overview.summary: The 2026 U.S. midterm elections are the nationwide federal elections held halfway through the four-year presidential term. Voters will choose all members of the U.S. House of Representatives and a regularly scheduled class of U.S. senators, alongside state and local contests that vary by jurisdiction.

facts.label: Election date
facts.value: Federal congressional elections in 2026 are scheduled for Tuesday, November 3, 2026—the Tuesday after the first Monday in November in an even-numbered year.

facts.label: House elections
facts.value: All House seats are contested because the Constitution provides for Representatives to be chosen every second year.

facts.label: Senate elections
facts.value: The Senate has six-year terms staggered into three classes, so roughly one-third of Senate seats are normally up for election in each even-numbered year.

facts.label: New congressional term
facts.value: The members elected in 2026 will take office at noon on January 3, 2027, under the Twentieth Amendment and the federal election-date statute.

facts.label: Administration and rules
facts.value: Federal elections are administered through decentralized state and local systems: state law generally governs procedures, subject to the U.S. Constitution and federal election laws, and local jurisdictions commonly conduct and certify elections.

event_overview.title: About Climate Change
event_overview.subject: Climate Change
event_overview.summary: Climate change refers to long-term shifts in Earth’s climate system, now driven principally by human greenhouse-gas emissions. It provides the broader context for reports of unusually high temperatures, flooding, and glacier change, while the contribution of climate change to any individual event requires event-specific scientific assessment.

facts.label: Heat and rainfall extremes
facts.value: The IPCC finds that hot extremes, including heatwaves, have become more frequent and intense across most land regions since the 1950s, and that human-caused climate change has contributed to heavier precipitation at the continental scale in Europe.

facts.label: Glaciers
facts.value: Human influence is assessed as very likely to be the main driver of global glacier retreat since the 1990s, a relevant long-term context for reporting on Himalayan glacier risks.

facts.label: International framework
facts.value: The UN Framework Convention on Climate Change was adopted on May 9, 1992 and entered into force on March 21, 1994; its stated ultimate objective is to prevent dangerous human interference with the climate system.

facts.label: Paris Agreement
facts.value: The Paris Agreement was adopted on December 12, 2015 and entered into force on November 4, 2016. It aims to hold warming well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows several 2026 reports concerning heat, flooding, glaciers, and global temperature records; it does not catalogue all climate impacts or establish causation for each individual weather event.

explore_lenses.title: It extends an exceptional heat period
explore_lenses.summary: August was not just the warmest August in Copernicus's ERA5 record; it tied July 2023 as the warmest month across all calendar months. claims.text: Copernicus measured a global average surface-air temperature of 16.96°C in August 2026, 0.85°C above the 1991–2020 August average; it tied July 2023 for the warmest month in the ERA5 record.

Copernicus's Samantha Burgess said the concurrent atmospheric and ocean records show climate change is driving extremes with growing consequences for communities, economies and ecosystems.

While some reports described it as the hottest month on record, Copernicus’s ERA5 analysis put the global average at 16.96°C—0.85°C above the 1991–2020 August norm—and tied it with July 2023 as the warmest month in that record. sections.heading: Human warming and ocean heat
sections.body: Scientists attribute the heat surge largely to human-caused climate change. The IPCC assesses that human influence has unequivocally warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land since pre-industrial times. Copernicus also reported record August sea-surface temperatures outside the polar oceans, including exceptional warmth in the tropical Pacific, as well as record-high global land temperatures for August.

sections.heading: Warming trend extends beyond August
sections.body: The June-to-August global average tied 2024 as the warmest boreal summer on record, according to Copernicus. The September 2025-to-August 2026 average was 1.48°C above the estimated 1850–1900 baseline. Through January to August, 2026 ranked as the second-warmest year on record; Copernicus said the annual average would be close to 2024’s record if the final four months matched the warmth of the same period in 2023.

sections.heading: El Niño raises weather risks
sections.body: The World Meteorological Organization said El Niño was expected to intensify into a very strong event before peaking near the end of 2026, with nearly a 100% likelihood of persisting through February 2027. event_overview.title: About Israeli Settlements
event_overview.subject: Israeli Settlements
event_overview.summary: Israeli settlements are Israeli civilian communities established in territory Israel captured in the 1967 war, chiefly in the West Bank and East Jerusalem. They are a central issue in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict because international bodies regard them as contrary to international law, while Israel argues that their final status is to be resolved through direct negotiations under the Oslo framework.

facts.label: Geography and history
facts.value: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) describes Israel’s ongoing settlement policy as operating in the West Bank and East Jerusalem; it notes that settlements also existed in Gaza from 1967 until Israel removed them in 2005.

facts.label: International legal position
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2334, adopted on December 23, 2016, states that Israeli settlements in Palestinian territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem, have “no legal validity” and calls for settlement activity to cease.

facts.label: ICJ advisory opinion
facts.value: In its July 19, 2024 advisory opinion, the ICJ concluded that Israel’s transfer of settlers to, and maintenance of their presence in, the West Bank and East Jerusalem is contrary to Article 49(6) of the Fourth Geneva Convention.

facts.label: Oslo-era administration
facts.value: Israel’s government says the Oslo Accords left settlements as a permanent-status issue and assigned Israel governing powers and jurisdiction in Area C of the West Bank, where many settlements and security installations are located, pending final-status negotiations.

facts.label: International dealings
facts.value: Resolution 2334 calls on states to distinguish, in relevant dealings, between the territory of Israel and territories occupied since 1967; this distinction is a key basis for governmental measures directed at settlement-linked persons, entities, goods, or activities rather than Israel generally.

facts.label: Senate elections
facts.value: The Senate has six-year terms staggered into three classes, so roughly one-third of Senate seats are normally up for election in each even-numbered year.

facts.label: New congressional term
facts.value: The members elected in 2026 will take office at noon on January 3, 2027, under the Twentieth Amendment and the federal election-date statute.

event_overview.title: About FIFA Elections
event_overview.subject: FIFA Elections
event_overview.summary: FIFA presidential elections are the process through which the FIFA Congress elects the president of world football’s governing body. The next scheduled election is due at the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco, where Gianni Infantino has said he will seek another term.

facts.label: Scheduled election
facts.value: The 77th FIFA Congress, designated by FIFA as the electoral event for the presidency, is scheduled for Thursday, 18 March 2027, in Rabat, Morocco.

facts.label: Electorate
facts.value: FIFA states that it has 211 member associations; its Congress is the body that elects the FIFA president.

facts.label: Term and limits
facts.value: The FIFA president is elected for a four-year term and may serve no more than three terms, whether consecutive or not.

facts.label: Election timing
facts.value: Under FIFA’s statutes, the presidential election is held in the year following a FIFA World Cup, and the elected president’s term begins after the Congress that elects them.

facts.label: Incumbent’s election history
facts.value: Infantino was first elected FIFA president at an Extraordinary Congress in Zurich on 26 February 2016 and was re-elected at the 73rd FIFA Congress in Kigali, Rwanda, in March 2023.
